repository.name: looper
repository.scope: entire repository (Go production + test code, excluding .git/.worktrees/.claude)

summary.verdict: A well-engineered, heavily-tested multi-role automation daemon with strong architectural boundaries and contract discipline. The primary structural risk is concentrated complexity in a few large runner/handler files and accumulated backward-compatibility layers in config normalization. No systemic correctness or security defects were found; the codebase is maintainable today with planned decomposition of its largest files.
strengths: Clean build: go vet, go build, staticcheck, and full test suite all pass
Strong test discipline: 129K lines of tests vs 109K lines of production Go code
Well-defined role boundaries with extracted workflow packages per role
SQLite migration system with embedded manifests and compatibility validation
Hot-reload config with curated allowlist prevents unsafe runtime changes
Trusted review proxy pattern isolates credentials from agent processes
Process containment and execution supervisor for agent lifecycle
Structured error types and sentinel errors throughout
Authority-conscious design: explicit ownership of declarations vs execution
risks: fixer/runner.go at 8,768 lines is a complexity hotspot with mixed responsibilities
api/handler.go at 7,706 lines couples HTTP transport with business logic
Panic calls in hot_reload.go and projects/view.go can crash the daemon on recoverable errors
Config normalization carries legacy merge layers that increase cognitive load
Each role redefines QueueFailureKind and step constants independently
limitations: E2E test harness code was excluded from detailed analysis
No performance profiling or load testing was performed
No security audit of webhook handling or credential flow was done

dimensions.name: Correctness and reliability
dimensions.summary: Strong correctness posture. The codebase uses explicit state machines, atomic transactions, and durable checkpoints. Recovery paths are well-tested. The main risk is panic-on-error in config reload paths, which can turn recoverable errors into crashes.
evidence: internal/storage/db.go:170 — WithTransaction wraps recover() and re-panics after rollback, correct pattern
internal/runtime/runtime.go:3874 — normalizeStaleQueuedLoopStatus handles all run status cases
internal/fixer/runner.go:1498 — New runner with Options pattern, dependency injection
internal/config/hot_reload.go:455 — panic on clone failure in hot-reload path is a recoverable error
internal/storage/embedded_migrations.go:31 — mustLoadEmbeddedMigrations panics on startup invariant failure, acceptable

dimensions.name: Understandability
dimensions.summary: Naming and structure are generally clear, but the size of key files (fixer/runner.go 8.7K, api/handler.go 7.7K) increases cognitive load. Config normalization has accumulated legacy merge functions that are hard to trace.
evidence: internal/fixer/runner.go:43-58 — FixerStep aliases workflow.Step, clear delegation
internal/config/normalize.go:296 — mergePartialReviewerRoleDiscoveryWithCanonicalPriority has 4-level conditional nesting
internal/api/handler.go:92-124 — Context struct has 15+ function fields, high surface area
internal/runtime/scheduler.go:42-139 — Interface-based role abstractions are well-named
internal/triager/runner.go:104-121 — Report struct documents its own authority clearly

dimensions.name: Maintainability
dimensions.summary: Change isolation is good within roles but the scheduler couples all roles. Config changes require touching load/normalize/validate across multiple files. Legacy compatibility layers add friction.
evidence: internal/runtime/scheduler.go:42-87 — Scheduler holds interfaces to 7+ role schedulers, changes propagate
internal/config/normalize.go:338 — mergeConfig touches 12+ sub-merge functions per config change
internal/config/hot_reload.go:135 — hotReloadCompatibilityPaths is a second registry alongside hotEditablePaths
internal/fixer/runner.go:2660 — executeStep dispatches to per-step handlers, good isolation
internal/storage/repositories.go:77 — NewRepositories constructs all repos, centralized

dimensions.name: Design and modularity
dimensions.summary: Strong role-based modularity with clear boundaries. Each role has its own workflow package. The storage layer uses a clean repository pattern. The webhook forwarder uses lane-based routing. The main weakness is the size of the top-level runner files.
evidence: internal/fixer/workflow/workflow.go:158 — Extracted workflow authority, 158 lines
internal/reviewer/workflow/workflow.go — Same pattern for reviewer
internal/worker/workflow/workflow.go — Same pattern for worker
internal/webhookforward/forwarder.go:34-42 — Lane-based routing with clear enum
internal/daemonservice/service.go:1-38 — Explicit Authority and Contract documentation
internal/agent/executor.go:96-136 — ExecutorOptions with clear ownership semantics

dimensions.name: Testability and verification
dimensions.summary: Excellent test coverage. Test code exceeds production code. Interfaces are widely used for mocking. Test files are co-located. The test suite passes in ~300s.
evidence: internal/fixer/runner_test.go:8191 lines vs runner.go:8768 lines
internal/api/handler_test.go:8453 lines vs handler.go:7706 lines
internal/runtime/runtime_test.go:5102 lines vs runtime.go:3934 lines
internal/config/config_test.go:4163 lines for config package
go test ./... — all packages pass

dimensions.name: Security
dimensions.summary: Good security posture. Trusted review proxy isolates credentials. Agent env is filtered. Process containment is enforced. Webhook admission is gated. No hardcoded secrets found.
evidence: internal/agent/executor.go:44-61 — unsafeAgentEnvKeys blocklist prevents git env injection
internal/runtime/scheduler.go:349-382 — mintTrustedReviewProxyForPR binds credentials to specific PR
internal/agent/executor.go:122 — Owner field admits spawn under Execution Supervisor
internal/webhookforward/forwarder.go:143 — AllowExecute gate at accept time
internal/api/handler.go:785 — authorizeRequest with auth mode check

dimensions.name: Performance and resource use
dimensions.summary: No performance issues observed. SQLite is configured with connection limits. Discovery caching is in place. Webhook forwarding uses bounded queues. No measurements were taken.
evidence: internal/storage/db.go:16-18 — sqliteMaxOpenConnections=4, busy timeout 5s
internal/infra/github/gateway.go:80 — DiscoveryCacheTTL for list caching
internal/webhookforward/forwarder.go:26 — defaultQueueCapacity=128, defaultMaxConcurrent=4
internal/runtime/scheduler.go:99 — MaxConcurrentRuns limits parallelism

dimensions.name: Operability and consistency
dimensions.summary: Strong operability. Hot-reload config, structured logging, event log, recovery summaries, and status endpoints are all present. The daemon service install/uninstall is well-documented with explicit contracts.
evidence: internal/config/hot_reload.go:147 — IsHotEditablePath curated allowlist
internal/daemonservice/service.go:17-37 — Explicit Install/Uninstall contract
internal/runtime/runtime.go:50-84 — RecoverySummary with detailed classification
internal/api/handler.go:924 — buildHealthResponse for health checks
internal/storage/db.go:146 — Backup method on SQLiteCoordinator

root_causes.summary: Top-level runner files (fixer/runner.go, api/handler.go) accumulate responsibilities that span discovery, claiming, processing, publishing, and HTTP transport, making them harder to decompose incrementally.

score_effect.rationale: Two core files exceed 7,700 lines each, creating a coordinated decomposition burden.

root_causes.summary: Panic calls in runtime config reload and view clone paths treat recoverable errors as fatal, removing the operator's ability to diagnose and retry without a restart.

score_effect.rationale: Panics in recoverable paths are a localized defect but affect shared infrastructure.

root_causes.summary: Each role redefines QueueFailureKind, step constants, and PullRequestSummary/Detail types independently, creating parallel type hierarchies that must be kept in sync when shared semantics change.

score_effect.rationale: Parallel type definitions across roles require coordinated updates but are not a correctness risk.

findings.title: Replace panic in config hot-reload and view clone paths with error propagation
symptoms: 7 panic calls in hot_reload.go for JSON clone/compare failures
6 panic calls in projects/view.go for clone failures
1 panic in runtime.go mustMarshalJSON for event payload marshaling
counterexamples: A corrupted or unusually large config file triggers a daemon crash instead of a reload error
violated_invariants: Recoverable runtime errors must not crash the daemon process
findings.evidence: hot_reload.go:455 panics on json.Clone failure; this is a recoverable error that should be returned to the caller and reported as a reload failure.
findings.impact: A single config file read error or JSON marshaling edge case can crash the entire daemon, losing all in-flight work.
findings.recommendation: Return errors from clone/compare helpers and propagate them through the reload chain. Log and report reload failures via the existing config reload status mechanism.

findings.title: Decompose fixer/runner.go into cohesive sub-packages
symptoms: Mixed discovery, claiming, processing, publishing, and recovery logic
violated_invariants: A file should have one coherent reason to change
findings.evidence: The file already extracts workflow, reconcile, publish, and failurepolicy sub-packages. The remaining 8.7K lines handle discovery, claiming, dirty adoption, terminal cleanup, and followup threads — each a candidate for extraction.
findings.impact: High cognitive load for fixer-related changes; increased risk of regressions when modifying unrelated fixer behavior.
findings.recommendation: Extract discovery, dirty-adoption, and terminal-cleanup into separate packages under internal/fixer/, leaving the runner as a thin orchestrator.

findings.title: Decompose api/handler.go into route-group handlers
symptoms: Context struct carries 15+ function fields for all handler dependencies
violated_invariants: HTTP transport should be separable from business logic
findings.evidence: The file handles health, status, config, loops, webhooks, logs, retry/discard, and worker occupancy in a single Handler struct. Sub-files exist for config_patch, loop_logs_stream, loop_retry_discard, but the main handler remains monolithic.
findings.impact: API changes require navigating a 7.7K-line file; testing requires constructing the full Context.
findings.recommendation: Split into per-route-group handler structs (healthHandler, configHandler, loopHandler) sharing a common dependencies struct.

findings.title: Consolidate role step and failure-kind types into shared packages
symptoms: Each role defines QueueFailureKind with identical constants
Each role defines its own PullRequestSummary/Detail structs
Step constants are aliased from workflow packages but re-exported
violated_invariants: Shared semantics should have a single declaration
findings.evidence: internal/fixer/runner.go:60-81, internal/reviewer/runner.go:92-98, internal/worker/runner.go:49-58 all define FailureRetryableTransient etc.
findings.impact: Adding a new failure kind requires touching 4+ role packages; drift is possible.
findings.recommendation: Extract shared failure kinds and step types into internal/roles or internal/workflow packages. Keep role-specific extensions as wrappers.

findings.title: Reduce config normalization legacy merge complexity
symptoms: Multiple merge* functions for reviewer, fixer, worker, planner roles
hotReloadCompatibilityPaths is a second registry alongside hotEditablePaths
violated_invariants: Configuration should have one clear precedence order
findings.evidence: normalize.go:242-335 shows three merge functions for reviewer config alone, each handling canonical vs legacy field priority.
findings.impact: Understanding the effective config for a role requires tracing through multiple merge passes.
findings.recommendation: Document the merge precedence as a contract test. Consider a generic merge helper with field-level priority annotations.

findings.title: mustMarshalJSON panics on JSON marshaling failure
symptoms: panic(err) in mustMarshalJSON for event payload marshaling
counterexamples: A deeply nested or circular event payload could trigger a marshal panic
violated_invariants: Event logging must not crash the daemon
findings.evidence: runtime.go:3900-3905 panics on json.Marshal failure. Event payloads are controlled by the codebase, so this is low-risk but violates the 'no panic on recoverable errors' principle.
findings.impact: A bug in event payload construction could crash the daemon instead of being caught at development time.
findings.recommendation: Return error from mustMarshalJSON (rename to marshalJSON) and handle at call sites, or use a development-time assertion.

checks.summary: All packages pass (storage 11s, runtime 33s, worker 12s, fixer/reviewer/planner/coordinator/triager all pass)

items: Replace panic in hot_reload.go and projects/view.go with error propagation (CQ-001)
Replace panic in mustMarshalJSON with error return (CQ-002)
Decompose fixer/runner.go into discovery, dirty-adopt, and terminal-cleanup packages (DM-001)
Consolidate role step and failure-kind types into shared packages (MN-001)
Reduce config normalization legacy merge complexity (UM-002)
